Co-op Dark Souls but with guns. (Around 40hrs playtime)

Very replayable. If you don't like the current world location/difficulty then you can reroll until needed. There's one particular world where we've rerolled at least 4 times and still stumble across something new everytime. Puzzles are also fun to solve. Some puzzles are numerical or pattern based; while others are skill or perceptive based. Minor Puzzle Spoiler: [spoiler]One puzzle requires you to know how to read music off a sheet and copy the pattern (playing an instrument irl helped).[/spoiler] Difficulty varies from person to person but having at least 3 people in your group would be wise for higher level difficulties.

FROMSOFTWARE fans beware: Rolling is slightly different. It requires you to roll BEFORE an attack instead of during to get a "perfect roll." So you'll have to rewire/purge your dodge habits a bit.



Update: Still AMAZING (112hrs playtime)

     I've been playing with a friend and we played and rerolled maps dozens of times. We started on the easiest difficulty and have made our way all the way to Apocalypse (hardest mode). I said previously that three people would be best for higher difficulty, but we are managing fine. Three would still be best so one can draw aggro while the other can revive or heal. The higher the difficulty, the higher the damage enemies do and the less damage you deal (or so it seems). Bosses on easy mode are melted within a minute, but Apocalypse bosses can take up to 20 minutes depending on what traits they have. On top of that, some of them hit so hard we're required to have some sort of healing class each to keep up. It's not that bad though, the rewards for higher difficulty are also pretty juicy.

     One of the best things about this game is the almost infinite amount of builds you can create. You can be a summoner who heals faster than can take damage, a teleporting tank, make everything bleed, become a sith lord, infinitely incinerate everything, chronomancy, and my friend's personal fav: fart on everyone and everything until nobody's standing. 

Of course a game like this has a few Cons to it:

1. RNG Gods: The randomness is amazing. After rerolling each word a minimum of 6 or 7 times, we still came across new things. We played blind on the first run through, but started looking things up after that. We read about items and wanted them... only to find them after rerolling the worlds multiple times. That part wasn't pleasant. Fun, but not pleasant. Trying to find an item, dungeon, or boss only to not get it was rather annoying. One particular boss,  [spoiler] The Custodian's Eye, in N'Erud [/spoiler], only spawned once in our entire game play and it took about 5 rerolls to run across it.

2. Fall Damage: It's very random and chaotic. We though it was due to armor, weight, or height... but it was so inconsistent. It was never enough to be annoying, it was still enough for us to scratch our heads on. One of us would jump off a balcony and the other doing the same. One would land with no fall damage while the other would lose half their health. Other times, we would jokingly through ourselves off ledge to kill ourselves on the rocks below other for one of us to survive without damage on a certainly lethal fall. Very inconsistent, but not too invasive during gameplay.

3. "Fixed" Glitches: As of 9/3/23, some of these glitches have been supposedly noticed and fixed. A few of the achievements in the game aren't working for a lot of players. The rest of this might be spoilers and a bit of whining so I'll place a spoiler tag over this paragraph. [spoiler] One of the bugged achievements is reaching max trait points and my friend an I have reach maximum trait points since the first two weeks after release. I got my achievement but he still hasn't gotten his achievement. Another one is the Leto's Stash. I was dead and spectating wwhen my firend discovered it, but maybe for that reason, I didn't get the achievement. The last ome is the Red Room. This requires opening a secret vault that can only be open during a Blood Moon. We knew how to open it and triggered many blood moons... but the doors never opened. [/spoiler] I'm been aiming to complete this game's achievements and I have 47/50 done. Two are just bugged while the other I'm working on. Mildly annoying.


Edit: These achievement glitches are fixed. 10/10 game.

This game blew me away, I don't know what I was expecting going into it, I played the first game and had fun with it but it wasn't really a memorable experience for me. But this was an absolute blast, and in my opinion one of the best games to come out this year.

I played a co-op campaign and solo campaign both of which on Nightmare difficulty.

+ The music slaps, each boss fight felt unique and engaging in some way.
+ There's a ton of variations in the worlds and what bosses you can encounter. 
+ The game really encourages you to look in every nook and corner and a lot of times there's something there for your time.
+ There's actually some pretty interesting stories in each of the worlds
+The last boss was very challenging and one of the coolest fights I've seen in gaming in a long time, I haven't encountered a fight that felt unfair.
+ Co-op play is super fun (minus the negative stated below) and there's a good bit of party-supportive items and abilities you can use to synergize and strategize.

That being said the game wasn't perfect. 
- The first couple of days (Ultimate edition early access at the least) had issues with performance and the latency in multiplayer is rough to deal with but eventually I got used to it and could play around it, naturally it'd be better if they fixed it to be more client sided. 
- There's some issues with inputs. Particularly when you're trying to quickly resurrect your teammates and you kind of have to stand next to your teammate and wait for the prompt to press 'E' on them shows up. Or if some ammo is nearby and you pick up the ammo instead of ressing them.
- The (weapon) mods in the game felt fairly underwhelming except for a couple of them. Firestorm comes to mind and there's not many situations I wouldn't use it in favor of other mods. This could just be my preference though.
- The same as stated above for weapons, however, mainly its just that swapping weapons feels not worth it because you need to level them in order for them to be worth using over your current weapon. Not sure how this should be addressed it just feels unfortunate that I'm discouraged from trying different weapons. 

For performance  : I have since tried AMD FSR - performance (i7 7700k / 32gb RAM / 1080ti) and I went from a struggling framerate to a very comfortable rate, I'm not one to nitpick looks in a game because I don't really care. If you're having issues with performance try messing with FSR or DLSS. Helped me, might help you.

The base game is incredible and solo play is a ton of fun, especially when experimenting with guns and archetype combos. With a bit of post launch patches to address some of the issues that people are having they can really hit a homerun. Especially since they have quite a few DLCs planned.

Remnant II is essentially a more realised version of Remnant : From the Ashes. A game that emphasises secret finding and exploration, nearly every outing is a fresh adventure in of itself. What you find is a complete potluck but it hits more than misses more often than not. It can be a difficult game at times but luckily you can eventually develop strategies to make the game's difficulty trivialised at least at the moment.

The worldbuilding is strong, really really strong. Each world is unique in of itself, a completely built from the ground up world filled with it's own unique lore. Each world has different ideals and is going through a different crisis in of themselves. It makes you feel like you could literally go ANYWHERE in remnant's universe. This applies to both this game and it's previous one. Yes, one of the worlds is a rehash of a previous one from the original but it's expanded. The world has moved on from it's place in the original in a big drastic way. This civilisation has been thrown into anarchy by an apocalypse and you're seeing the effects in real time. Your actions in the first game affect the world, it's people and the reaction to yourself as a human. It's also a bit more hopeful of a game than the original. The first game i'd argue was amazingly bleak and while it can be just as bleak in remnant II at times, it's given a bit of hope here. I'd say this is by far the strongest thing the game gets right. Realising these worlds and their massive shifts in artstyles is frankly an achievement in of itself, it's factored even into gameplay through exploration. 

The gameplay i'd say is still just as fun as Remnant : From the Ashes but starkly similar with the exception of the unique class Archetypes (Which allows you to fashion yourself a bit more instead of being pigeonholed into armor set bonuses, like FRA.), Relic changes and overall approach to the world structure. It's a lot less linear than Remnant : From the Ashes. You have a lot of space to explore compared to the original. The enemies are something i have a small grievance with. Certain enemies have almost identical attacks to ones in Remnant : From the Ashes to the point where it's glaringly obvious they are just recycled enemies. This isn't an enormous issue as i feel Remnant II does enough to make itself standout as a sequel but it's still mildly annoying. It can also sometimes feel like going through the same motions that you did in Remnant : From the Ashes. If you liked a playstyle in that game, it's very likely to be an option in this one. Right down to certain armor sets from the original game returning. I'll leave it to you to find out which. There are many different playstyles to pick from that definitely have fancy bells and whistles building on the strengths of what people liked in niche builds from Remnant : From the Ashes. 

Melee. Melee in the original Remnant was fairly underwhelming. You couldn't really work them into your builds but in Remnant II they are FANTASTIC close range options for enemies that love getting in your face but do not invalidate your firearms as flying enemies and enemies that deliberately stay out of your close range will wreck you if you opt for that playstyle. If you wanna be a stoic space marine with a alien rocket hammer then this is your jam.

I'm not entirely convinced on an outright recommendation right now because i would love more story variety for each of the worlds when you re-run them. I'm not going to spoil too much there but it's around 2 for each of the 3 mainline worlds. They are good and are drastically unique from each other in objectives but once you've seen them both then you just have the random events which it feels there are a lot less of in this game. Bosses included. Remnant : From the Ashes had a staggering amount of unique encounters and bosses. To the point where i could say you could run through a world three or four times and still only barely get halfway through what you have seen. It feels like there just isn't as much there. Maybe it's because the game has two smaller worlds with less variation even with fantastic bosses in them that the mainline worlds don't get as much side content. 

If you overwhelmingly enjoyed Remnant : From the Ashes it's a no brainer, get the game. It's good fun but if you are a newer player and are looking for a very similar game with a tons more content to explore and enjoy then i would get Remnant : From the Ashes for now. When you come back to this game, it'll likely have so much more to do and enjoy and you'll also have the added context from the previous game to add onto this one.
